prompt.context: Your client is the CEO of a semiconductor material manufacturer. The product they sell are 'lead frames', which is a technology that emerged in the 1970s and is a core component to build electronic components such as ICs used in automotive solutions. The client is in Asia and most of their customers are global chip manufacturers for automotive and consumer electronics (NXP, IDT, etc.). The client's company is a subsidiary of a global conglomerate, and the conglomerate's HQ sets annual goals for all subsidiaries. Among many parameters the most weight is given to OP (operating profit) and Revenue Growth. The client did not meet last year's goal and is asking you, the main consultant, for ways to achieve this year's (2020) goal.
prompt.question: What recommendations would you make to help the client achieve their 2020 goal of operating profit and revenue growth that are 2pp above the industry average?

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's specific goal?
clarifying_info.a: 2pp over the industry average for both OP and Revenue Growth.

clarifying_info.q: What are the 2020 targets vs. actuals/forecasts?
clarifying_info.a: Industry average: OP 11.0%, Growth 0%. Goal: OP 13.0%, Growth 2.0%. Client forecast: OP 11.0%, Growth 0.9%.
Industry average: OP 8.8%, Growth -6.9%. Goal: OP 10.8%, Growth -4.9%. Client actual: OP 9.5%, Growth -6.4%.
Industry average: OP 7.3%, Growth 7.7%. Goal: OP 9.3%, Growth 9.7%. Client actual: OP 6.0%, Growth 9.0%.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have a global presence?
clarifying_info.a: Client main office is in Taiwan. 80% of revenue comes through local agents and distributors who charge 3% commission on the final price.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have more than one factory?
clarifying_info.a: One factory only in Taiwan, with 20-30% idle capacity. They did not see the need for another factory.

clarifying_info.q: What are the main cost components?

clarifying_info.a: They are looking into new technologies/businesses, but it is forecasted to take at least 5 years for revenue to materialize. Currently new businesses represent less than 0.5% of revenue.
The time of this case is late 2019, so COVID-19 was not a thing. The case ignores the effect of COVID-19.

exhibits.title: 2020 Lead Frame Forecasted Revenue and Operating Profit
exhibits.shows: A bubble chart plotting the top 6 players in the Lead frame market (including the client). The x-axis is YoY Revenue Growth (%), the y-axis is Operating Profit (%), and bubble size represents Revenue ($M). Reference lines mark the Industry Average Growth (0.0%) and Industry Average OP (11.0%). The client's bubble is labeled with $237M revenue.

data.x_axis: YoY Revenue Growth (%), range approx -1.0% to 5.0%
data.note: Client target is 2pp over industry average. Biggest bubble (Competitor A) revenue is $352M.

framework: Meet Client's Goal: OP and Revenue Growth 2pp above industry average
Increase Revenue — two sub-buckets: (1) Current customers / core business; (2) New customers / new business

Increase Operating Profit (cut costs) — separate buckets: (1) Material costs (copper, 50%); (2) Labor costs (30%); (3) Logistics costs; (4) Agent/distributor costs (3% commission — extra credit bucket)

questions.prompt: Analyze Exhibit 1. What does the chart tell you about the client's competitive position and whether the goal is being met?
questions.guidance: A strong analysis covers: (1) State the goal (2pp over industry average = OP 13%, Growth 2%). (2) Client is above industry average in revenue growth (1pp above at ~1%) but only on par in OP (11% = industry average). Therefore the client is failing to achieve the goal on both dimensions. (3) Bubble size: all 6 top players have similar bubble sizes; client appears to be one of the smallest among the top 6. (4) YoY Revenue: range is roughly -0.5% to 5% among top 6; extra credit — since most top 6 are above average growth, smaller players must be showing negative growth. (5) OP: most top 6 cluster around the industry average, consistent with this being a materials/upstream business with little differentiation.

questions.prompt: Assuming the client meets the 2% revenue growth target and keeps absolute operating costs constant, how much additional cost must be saved to also meet the 13% OP target?
questions.guidance: Walk candidate from revenue to operating costs step by step. Key formula: Operating Costs = Revenue × (1 - Operating Profit %). If candidate struggles, hint that the $237M revenue already reflects 1% growth, so they need to recalculate revenue at 2% growth first.

math.setup: 2020 Revenue (given, at 1% growth): $237.0M. Derive 2019 revenue then re-grow at 2%. Operating Costs = Revenue × (1 - OP%).
steps: 2020 Operating Costs at current OP of 11% = 237 × 0.89 = $211.0M
2020 Target Operating Costs at OP of 13% with 2% revenue = 239.4 × 0.87 = $208.3M
math.answer: The client needs to cut an additional $2.7M in operating costs to reach the 13% OP target, assuming 2% revenue growth is achieved.

brainstorming.prompt: It is mid-March 2020. Just as you are about to submit your proposal to the client, you hear that industry specialists are revising their forecasts due to the COVID-19 pandemic having real global impact. While most industry growth rates are revised to 'minus growth', the semiconductor industry's growth rate is being forecasted higher than before. Especially for Lead frames, the forecast has been revised from 0% to +5% revenue growth. What do you think may be the reason for this phenomenon? Optional follow-up: How would this increased growth rate change your proposal to the client?

categories.name: Value Chain: Materials (Copper)
ideas: Price of copper may have dropped due to decreased global demand, lowering input costs for lead frame manufacturers

categories.name: Value Chain: Client's Customers (Semiconductor Manufacturers)
ideas: Disruption of supply chains may have caused chip manufacturers to hoard upstream materials (lead frames) to keep manufacturing lines running and prevent shortages

categories.name: Value Chain: End Customers (Electronics Users)
ideas: Huge demand increase driven by shift to virtual work/life — PCs, webcams, data centers, and servers all require more semiconductors
Electric Vehicles and Autonomous Driving are increasing electronic content per vehicle rapidly

categories.name: Industry Sensitivity
ideas: Automotive and electronics industries are less sensitive to social distancing effects compared to retail and tourism
Lead frames are upstream in the value chain; COVID-19 demand effects may reach upstream suppliers later, but must still have a reason for the upward trend

recommendation: The client is close to achieving the 2020 goal. A 1pp improvement in revenue growth (from ~1% to 2%) and a ~$2.7M reduction in operating costs (representing approximately a 2pp OP improvement) are required and appear achievable.
On revenue: focus on expanding sales to current customers (leveraging idle factory capacity of 20-30%) and selectively targeting new customers in adjacent segments.

On cost reduction: priority levers are (1) renegotiating copper material costs — the largest cost bucket at 50%; (2) labor efficiency improvements; (3) reviewing and potentially reducing agent/distributor commissions (currently 3% of final price on 80% of revenue).

Updated for COVID context: the revised forecast of +5% industry growth significantly improves the revenue outlook and makes the revenue growth target easier to achieve, which in turn may make the OP target easier to reach even without cost cuts.
risks: Semiconductor industry is cyclical — growth may not materialize as forecast
Client is one of the smallest players among the top 6; pricing power may be limited
Diversification into new businesses will not contribute to 2020 targets (5-year horizon)
Agent/distributor relationships may be difficult to renegotiate without losing sales coverage
next_steps: Conduct detailed copper procurement analysis and identify renegotiation leverage
Analyze customer pipeline to quantify near-term revenue growth potential
Model impact of reducing agent/distributor commissions on net revenue and relationships
Revise full-year 2020 model with updated COVID-era growth assumptions
